manifest.name: The governing text for the Tending view and the findings record

context.rationale:
PR #849 makes tending store what it concludes as findings in the notes store and shows them in a Tending view and beside their subjects in Activity. The code is committed; these are the documents that state the behavior, held uncommitted by the consent gate until you decide. They make three claims the code now enforces: an assessment is not the work (a finding stays open while a step is outstanding), a settled finding stays checked (its witnesses are read on every pass and every view load), and the browser and the command line apply one witness rule. They also take branch deletion out of tend, since a cloud session cannot do it. Approve the set, approve with edits, or return it.

NO BRANCH DIFF FOR THESE: each item carries its whole patch, and the exact patch for the set, generated files included, is approvals/2026-10-01-tending-governing-text.patch, which applies to the base named here with git apply.

items.title: docs/views/tending.md

change.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+# Tending (`?view=tending`)
+
+The **Tending** view lists what tending passes concluded about the estate's
+work: branches, pull requests, tracker tasks, snags and session records. Its
+unit is a **finding**, not an alert. A finding names the subjects it concerns,
+says why it matters, recommends a next step, and isolates the one choice that
+needs the owner, when there is one. Component:
+`lib/alpineComponents/tending.js`. Record and fold: `lib/kits/findings.js`.
+
+## The record
+
+A finding is a note in the registry's notes store (`notes/notes.jsonl`, the
+[notes skill](../../skills/notes/SKILL.md)) that carries a `finding` object:
+
+| Field | Holds |
+| --- | --- |
+| `kind` | Provisional vocabulary: `unreached` (useful work that never reached the owner), `answer` (one specific answer needed), `overlap` (separate efforts that could be brought together), `superseded` (the work landed or was overtaken elsewhere). The view labels these and shows any other kind by name. |
+| `subjects` | Locators for everything the finding concerns: `owner/repo#N`, `owner/repo@branch`, `owner/repo:path` for a task or file, `owner/repo:docs/SNAGS.md#slug`, and a session's record file in the registry. The note's `about` is the first subject. |
+| `why`, `next`, `choice` | Why it matters, the recommended next step, and the owner's question with a recommendation. A step only the owner may take, such as closing a pull request, is a `choice`. |
+| `evidence` | Short verifiable facts: commits, files, pull requests, dates. |
+| `witnesses` | Pinned references ([locators.md](../locators.md)), including things outside the subjects whose change would change the conclusion (table below). |
+
+**An assessment is not the work.** A finding is open while it carries an
+outstanding `next` or `choice`, whatever its kind: "this pull request was
+overtaken" is a finished assessment and an unfinished job until someone closes
+the pull request. It is settled when nothing remains, either because the
+assessment needed no action or because a reply records it done.
+
+**Only a reply that carries `finding` changes a finding.** A tending pass
+reassesses by replying with new fields or witnesses; it settles one with
+`status: "settled"` and `did` (what was done), or renews attention with
+`status: "open"` and a new `next`. The owner closes one from the view with
+**Handled** (`status: "resolved"`) and reverses that with **Reopen**. A reply
+without `finding` is a comment: it is listed in the finding's history and
+changes nothing, however recent. An update replaces each field it carries
+whole.
+
+| Witness | Pins | Changed when |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `owner/repo@ref` with `sha` | a branch's tip | the tip is another commit; broken if the branch is gone |
+| `owner/repo@ref` with `contains` | a commit the ref must contain | the ref no longer contains it (`main` is pinned this way, never by its tip) |
+| `owner/repo@ref:path` with `sha` | the blob or tree at that path | the object at that path differs; broken if the path is gone |
+| `owner/repo#N` with `state` | a pull request's state | the state differs, or an open one was updated since |
+
+The browser and `findings.py check` apply this one rule, stated once as cases
+in `tools/test/findings.test.mjs`.
+
+## The view
+
+- **Attention** holds every finding with work outstanding, a question for the
+  owner first, then by kind and newest, **and any settled finding whose
+  evidence has since changed**, marked so, until a pass reassesses it.
+  **Settled** holds the rest, newest first, each saying what closed it:
+  nothing left to do, what tending did, or the owner's words.
+- A finding reads as a row: kind, title, the owner's call, the outstanding
+  next step, and its subjects as links (a pull request to GitHub, a branch to
+  the branch page, a session to its row in Sessions, a task or snag to its
+  file).
+- **A tap opens it:** why it matters, the evidence, each witness with its
+  verdict, the history (found, advanced, settled, handled, reopened, comments),
+  and the reply box with Handled, Reopen and Comment.
+- **Every finding's witnesses are checked on sight**, settled ones included:
+  a branch tip through the branches API, `contains` through the compare API,
+  a path through its folder's contents listing (which reports the blob or tree
+  sha `git rev-parse` would), and a pull request through the pulls API. A
+  witness that moved or broke puts **Changed since assessed** (or **Settled,
+  but changed since**) at the top of the finding, naming it.
+
+`?view=tending&tab=settled` opens Settled; `&item=<note id>` opens one finding
+with its details. A repo filter handed in from a Repos card is not stamped.
+
+## Beside the subjects
+
+The Activity panes show the same open findings where their subjects appear:
+
+- **Branches:** a line under each row an open finding names, by the branch or
+  by a pull request it heads, opening the finding here. The **Findings** scope
+  lists exactly those rows.
+- **Sessions:** the same line under a session whose record a finding names.
+- **Repos:** a count on each card of open findings touching the repo, by any
+  subject, opening this view narrowed to it.
+
+## Where findings come from
+
+A tending pass (the [tend skill](../../skills/tend/SKILL.md)) selects
+candidates mechanically, investigates them, and writes findings with
+`skills/tend/findings.py`:
+
+| Command | Does |
+| --- | --- |
+| `candidates` | Selects from `state/activity.json` and `state/sessions.json`: sessions that ended finished while their branch did not land, pull requests whose description holds a ✴️ ask, pull requests idle 30 days, non-Claude pull requests marked ready and idle. A candidate counts as covered only while the finding that names it holds: if one of its subjects moved after the assessment, it is due again, settled or not. |
+| `add` | Validates and writes a finding, refusing a witness that pins nothing checkable. |
+| `update` | Writes a reassessment as a reply carrying `finding`. |
+| `list` | Folds the findings: open ones, or every one with `--all`. |
+| `check` | Observes every witness of every finding, settled ones included (`--open` narrows), from the checkouts beside the store and the crawl's cache, and names the findings whose evidence moved. |
+
+The selection signals choose what to investigate. They are never shown as
+findings themselves.

items.commentary: New. The view's document: the finding record, the distinction between a finished assessment and finished work, how a finding changes, the four witness pins and what counts as a change to each, what Attention and Settled hold (including settled findings whose evidence moved), where Activity shows findings, and the findings.py commands.
